reviewer_blockers: 7.3-F1 (confirmed): the committed package's bundled SkiaSharp.dll + libSkiaSharp.so collide fatally with the host's own SkiaSharp, so the first ArrTags badge publication aborts the whole Jellyfin 12.0.0 process with System.InvalidCastException. GOALS.md criteria 5, 6, and 8 are not met as shipped and Phase 7 acceptance criteria 3 and 4 cannot be checked. Independently reproduced twice on the pinned host. Fixing this needs an architecture/packaging decision (new ADR) plus csproj/build.yaml/PluginPackagingTests changes and re-verification, so advancement to release is blocked.

findings.summary: Independently reproduced: the committed package's bundled duplicate SkiaSharp kills Jellyfin on the first badge publication; the finding is real, deterministic, and correctly attributed to the bundled copy, not to plugin logic.
findings.detail: Installed the unmodified artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip into /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0, pointed both providers at the committed mock fixture, created real Jellyfin Movie/Episode items with sidecar posters, and triggered a library refresh. The host exited with '[FTL] [20] Main: Unhandled Exception System.InvalidCastException: [A]SkiaSharp.UserDataDelegate cannot be cast to [B]SkiaSharp.UserDataDelegate', where A is the plugin-context copy at /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll (Emby.Server.Implementations.Plugins.PluginLoadContext #1) and B is the host default-context copy at /tmp/jf/jellyfin/SkiaSharp.dll; the stack is SkiaSharp.DelegateProxies.SKManagedStreamPeekProxyImplementation. It occurred ~1.9 s after the ArrTags post-scan task completed and left non-terminal artwork-operation records (MayHaveStartedMutation=true) for both items. A second fresh-state run reproduced the identical failure. Controls: removing only SkiaSharp.dll and libSkiaSharp.so from the installed plugin folder made the full pipeline work with 0 [FTL] (badges published and served, source sidecars byte-unchanged); with the full committed package but both providers disabled (so no publication occurs) the plugin still loaded the bundled SkiaSharp yet the refresh produced 0 [FTL]/InvalidCast and the host stayed up; with the plugin uninstalled the host serves items normally. The plugin-context load is explicit in the console: 'Loaded assembly SkiaSharp, Version=3.119.0.0 ... from /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll'. The host and plugin managed SkiaSharp.dll are byte-identical (sha256 aaaaa18c...), so this is a load-context type-identity conflict caused solely by shipping the duplicate, exactly as the worker reported.
evidence: Run 1 (both providers enabled, committed package): host process exited; /tmp/jf/console.log line 152 '[FTL] [20] Main: Unhandled Exception' + line 153 InvalidCastException [A] PluginLoadContext #1 /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll vs [B] Default /tmp/jf/jellyfin/SkiaSharp.dll; subsequent GET /System/Info/Public -> connection refused.
Run 2 (fresh state, both providers enabled, committed package): identical fatal InvalidCastException; host process gone.

Plugin-context load evidence: /tmp/jf/console.log 'Loaded assembly SkiaSharp, Version=3.119.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=0738eb9f132ed756 from /tmp/jf/data/plugins/ArrTags_0.1.0.0/SkiaSharp.dll' followed by 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0'.

Diagnostic control (only the two files removed from the installed plugin folder): POST /Library/Refresh -> 0 [FTL], host HTTP 200; GET /Items/792e65fe.../Images/Primary -> 200 image/png 14,845 B sha256 b23606a9... (== persisted artwork-state ActiveImageIdentity.ContentSha256); GET /Items/e26fb220.../Images/Primary -> 200 image/png 15,391 B sha256 fcba59c9... (== persisted ActiveImageIdentity).

Providers-disabled control (full committed package, both providers disabled): plugin loaded with the bundled SkiaSharp, refresh produced 0 [FTL]/InvalidCast, no provider requests, no artwork work, host up.
Uninstalled/normal-operation control: host scanned and served the items with no ArrTags installed; final clean restart reports 0 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags' and 0 [ERR]/[FTL].
Duplicate confirmed in the package: unzip -l artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip lists SkiaSharp.dll (489,824 B) and libSkiaSharp.so (11,170,296 B) at the plugin root.
findings.recommended_action: Do not release V1 from this package. Keep GOALS.md criteria 5, 6, 8 and Phase 7 acceptance criteria 3/4 unchecked and Gate 7 undeclared, and open a follow-up task with a new ADR to stop bundling the managed SkiaSharp.dll and native libSkiaSharp.so (share the host's SkiaSharp via the default load context), then update src/ArrTags/ArrTags.csproj (PackagePlugin target + SkiaSharp PackageReference assets), build.yaml artifacts, and the PluginPackagingTests that assert the bundled assets, and re-run this live verification against the committed package.

findings.summary: The task 4.8 research claim that the host's native libSkiaSharp.so is byte-for-byte identical to the NuGet asset does not hold on the pinned musl host (the managed SkiaSharp.dll is identical).
findings.detail: docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md section 2 records the spike host's libSkiaSharp.so as 11,170,296 bytes / sha256 66c856... and byte-identical to the NuGet SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.Linux 3.119.4 asset, measured against the glibc host at /tmp/opencode/jf. The pinned musl host /tmp/jf/jellyfin/libSkiaSharp.so is 18,453,464 bytes / sha256 59039b..., i.e. not the NuGet copy. The managed assembly is byte-identical (sha256 aaaaa18c...), so the blocker is still purely a duplicate-management problem, but the follow-up fix must be verified against the host's own native library rather than assumed byte-identical.
evidence: sha256sum /tmp/jf/jellyfin/SkiaSharp.dll = aaaaa18c68ba1f3a3408b00dff28b11d5705198e17ba9d3aa59222bfd35407c8 (same as the zip entry); AssemblyName version 3.119.0.0.

sha256sum /tmp/jf/jellyfin/libSkiaSharp.so = 59039b2548e3a3f563fa247f582c62d280c2015df78316fcab62e383d7ae9d4f (18,453,464 B) vs zip libSkiaSharp.so = 66c856eaf1a47a00b23204c30c6ee407987bf5086ecc0a1a6b4fd67526b0cd02 (11,170,296 B).
docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md section 2 records the spike host native asset as 11,170,296 B / 66c856...
findings.recommended_action: In the follow-up ADR/fix, re-verify host-SkiaSharp sharing against the pinned musl host's native library and correct the research/ADR record. No action for task 7.3.

findings.area: correctness / criterion 6 interaction (observed in the diagnostic install)
findings.summary: A full Jellyfin library metadata refresh re-imported the local sidecar poster and reverted a published badge while the plugin's persisted ActiveImageIdentity still recorded the badge as active.
findings.detail: In the first diagnostic run (committed-package duplicate removed) the plugin published badges: item ImageTags.Primary moved from ac2b726c/b7c66a45 to 680837a4/7c4ff71d and artwork-state recorded ActiveImageIdentity ContentSha256 B23606A9.../FCBA59C9.... A later POST /Library/Refresh restored the original sidecar images (item tags back to ac2b726c/b7c66a45; served bytes f380b2f9.../4b2e0f38...) while artwork-state still recorded the badge as active. This may be expected Jellyfin behavior when a local sidecar image exists and the plugin publishes into the metadata store; it could not be tested against the shipped package because that package crashes. The worker's criterion-6 run used the plugin's own reconcile task and did not show this.
evidence: Item ImageTags.Primary movie ac2b726c -> 680837a4 (after publication) -> ac2b726c (after POST /Library/Refresh); episode b7c66a45 -> 7c4ff71d -> b7c66a45.
artwork-state ActiveImageIdentity.ContentSha256 stayed B23606A9.../FCBA59C9... across the refresh while item ImageTags reverted to the sidecar tags.
findings.recommended_action: Worth confirming during follow-up fix verification whether a Jellyfin library refresh can silently revert a published badge while plugin state claims otherwise. No change required for task 7.3.

tests_checked: Independent live end-to-end reproduction on the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 musl host (not the product suites): committed package install, mock Sonarr/Radarr, real Jellyfin Movie/Series/Episode with sidecar posters - crash x2, diagnostic SkiaSharp-sharing control, providers-disabled control, Sonarr-only and Radarr-only provider isolation, changed/unchanged metadata, and a simulated provider outage.

Criteria 1-4 spot checks: 'Loaded plugin: ArrTags 0.1.0.0'; Sonarr-only run called only Sonarr endpoints, Radarr-only only Radarr, both-enabled called both (mock request log); persisted metadata-state recorded MatchStatus=0 (Matched) / MatchMethod=1 (ProviderId) with MatchedProviderIds Tmdb=990001 (movie, movie 1/file 11) and Tvdb=990004 (episode, series 1/episode 101/file 201); quality fields QualityLabel=Bluray-1080p/bluray/1080 and WEBDL-1080p/webdl/1080 with media-info resolution, dynamic range, codecs, channels, custom formats, upgrade-pending.

Criteria 5/6/8 spot checks under the diagnostic install: served image bytes equal to persisted ActiveImageIdentity (sha256 b23606a9.../fcba59c9...); source poster and thumbnail sidecars byte-unchanged (f380b2f9.../4b2e0f38...); a changed mock quality (1080p -> 2160p/HDR10) produced new metadata and publication fingerprints, a new image tag, and new served bytes; a true unchanged re-run left fingerprint/tag/bytes identical; a simulated outage left the host up (10/10 HTTP 200), the artwork unchanged, and metadata State=1 (stale) with no LastError.

Did not rerun the product test suites: src/ and tests/ are unchanged from the committed task 7.7 baseline, so the worker's reported counts cannot differ; they match the 7.7 baseline exactly (default Failed 0/Passed 1219/Skipped 60/Total 1279; host-guarded Failed 0/Passed 1235/Skipped 44/Total 1279).
Artifact check: artifacts/ArrTags_0.1.0.0.zip exists at the reported 5,475,666 bytes and contains ArrTags.dll, SkiaSharp.dll, libSkiaSharp.so, ArrTags.deps.json, build.yaml, notices and licenses.
research_checked: docs/research/skia-host-compatibility.md sections 2-3 (native asset facts, PluginLoadContext resolution): the load-context claim was verified live (the plugin folder SkiaSharp.dll is loaded into PluginLoadContext; the image processor runs against the host copy). The native byte-identity claim was found not to hold on the pinned musl host (finding F2).
